locator.text: Equation (C.8), p. 159, in the proof of Lemma C.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same inequality with the same U: coneBound P J = P + J²/4 − |J|√((P−2)/2 + J²/16) is exactly the smaller root in v of 2(P−v)² = (v−2)J² (checked: the roots are P + J²/4 ± |J|√((P−2)/2+J²/16)), and it is applied at P = p₁ + p₂·t, J = p₂ − p₁·t, i.e. the paper's P_c(t), J_c(t). Two rewritings. (i) Non-strict "2 + ε ≤" instead of "> 2 + δ_L": the margin is produced existentially with ε > 0, so 2 + ε ≤ U gives U > 2 + ε/2 and conversely. (ii) The compact family is indexed by the variance root r ∈ [0,R] rather than by the tilt amplitude μ ∈ [0,μ_max]: solvedTilt m d p r = extendedExpTilt m d (solveScale d p r) p, and μ ↦ scaledRoot d p μ is a strictly increasing bijection of [0,∞) with inverse solveScale (scaledRoot_strictMono, solveScale_spec, solveScale_unique), so the two index sets match after substitution, and R in uniform_tilt_cone_margin is universally quantified, so it may be taken large enough to cover [0,μ_max]. In the instantiation actually used (FamilyChoices, radius = √(3/aMin)) the range is the sub-family r ≤ √(3/aMin), which under the same substitution is a proper subset of μ ∈ [0,μ_max] because (C.7) is encoded as 3/aMin < tiltVariance d (p₂ x) maxAmplitude; it still contains the amplitude actually used (varianceRoot_bound).
